title: still present since round 4: EXEMPT_ARMS trusts comments over code — removing a claimed-unreachable arm's exit-path guard keeps the lint green
evidence:
lint_demo_network.py:44-46: `# Message arms whose real api calls are structurally unreachable in demo mode
# (auth flows always exit the demo first; ApiReturnedSession/PolicyRefresh are
# demo-guarded at the top of their handlers).` then `EXEMPT_ARMS = {` (:48) listing 18 constructor names (:49-70) with no mechanical verification of the claimed unreachability (contrast DEMO_INTERCEPTED, which is verified against demo_update.handle)
detail: The exemption list is justified only by its comment; the auth-arm claims (e.g. that login/logout always exit demo first) are not machine-checked like the interception manifest.
recommended_fix: Verify the auth-flow exit paths mechanically (interception or route-arm check), or shrink EXEMPT_ARMS to arms with verified guards.

title: still present since round 4: manifest matcher counts any capitalized constructor line in handle bodies as 'handled' (theoretical masking)
evidence:
lint_demo_network.py:274-280: `if in_case:
            stripped = line.strip()
            m = re.match(r"^([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]+)(\(| ->| \||$)", stripped)
            if m:
                handled.add(m.group(1))` — the scan is depth-tracked only for the closing brace; a capitalized constructor line nested inside an arm body (e.g. a comment-free `Some(x) ->` pattern or a constructor call at line start) also lands in `handled`
detail: A message could be counted as intercepted because its name appears nested in an arm body rather than as a top-level pattern — the manifest subset check would then pass vacuously.
recommended_fix: Restrict the pattern match to the case's top-level pattern depth (track brace depth per line before matching).

title: still present since round 4: CI fetch ban exempts the whole demo_api.gleam file, not just the documented download function
evidence: test.yml:135: `FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true)` — a file-level -v exemption; demo_api.gleam's only fetch use is download (:421 `use fetch_result <- promise.try_await(fetch.send(req))`)
detail: A second fetch call added anywhere else in demo_api.gleam passes CI despite the comment's "one documented static-PDF fetch" contract.
recommended_fix: Narrow the exemption to the download function (line-range or per-fn count), or bite-test a second fetch site.
